text: Welcome to Mazumgumso, African Scholarly Conversations, a podcast that highlights the perspectives of various stakeholders in academia and research fields across Africa through open dialogue for Mazumgumso on scholarly communication in Africa.

speaker: Joy Owango
text: Welcome to Mazumgumso, African Scholarly Conversations, where we are joined by an expansive list of African policymakers, science communication specialists, innovators, and tertiary institution leads who contribute to this realm of scholarly and science communication. I'm your host, Joy Owango, the Executive Director of the Training Center in Communication, Capacity Building Trust, based at the University of Nairobi, Kenya. In today's episode, we'll be exploring the growth of community-led open science initiatives in Africa, specifically focusing on efforts to improve the reproducibility and rigor of scientific research through local and collaborative networks. Joining us to discuss this in-depth is Emmanuel. And Emmanuel is a passionate African open science champion who has a keen interest in improving research culture across Africa. He is the founder of the African Reproducibility Network, AREN, a community-led initiative bridging the gaps in open science advocacy and adoption in Africa through training and local communities of practice. His journey in open science has led him working with organizations such as the Association of African Universities, AEU, eLife Publishers, the Center for Open Science, and several pro-open science organizations across the globe. He is currently one of the two co-directors of the Community Engagement Lead and the Community Engagement Lead at ARIN. Welcome, Emmanuel.

The model describes a very robust but flexible structure on how we can establish local communities of practice as institutions, both formally and informally, and with descriptions of what each role is doing and how they coordinate and collaborate. And then the model also establishes various national networks across the globe to ensure there is coordination across these countries. That's one of the reasons why we established a continent-wide community separate from or different from having these local networks at the institutions and research organizations. So that was what inspired us. But we did realize that if we decided to focus on only reproducibility, we would be missing a lot. We will not be really bridging the gap that we wanted to.
